deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page of doodles and diagrams, dated around December 1983. It follows page 1, 'Structure des dérivateurs', which posits for a derivator H and objects x,y in H(I) three levels of Hom: a set Hom, a homotopy type Homhot in Hot, and a relative version underline-Homhot in Hot(I). Page 1 also gives the adjunction formulas for f_!, f^*, f_*. The present page probes how to actually extract the homotopy type Homhot(x,y) from the bare derivator data.

(1) Lowest level. For x,y in H(e)=H(Δ0), set π0(x,y)=Hom_H(x,y).

(2) Next level. For a given f:x→y, he tries to define π1(x,y;f). The tool is the 'underlying diagram' functor H(Δ1)→H(Δ0)×H(Δ0), sending a coherent arrow to its source and target, with fibre over (x,y). The crossed-out start '= π0(Δ1 …' or 'Hom(Δ1…' suggests he wanted π1 as π0 or automorphisms of a fibre category of H(Δ1) over (x,y).
- The pictures support this reading: x⇉y with a 2-cell ⇓ between f and g, a labelled π1(x,y;f,g), and a 2-cell between 2-cells (⇛). These are homotopies, homotopies between homotopies, i.e. the cells of the mapping space.
- In modern terms, the fibre sequence Map(f,f) → Map(x,x)×Map(y,y) → Map(x,y) gives an exact sequence π1(End x × End y) → π1(Map(x,y),f) → Aut_{H(Δ1)}(f | id,id) → … So the derivator only sees π1 modulo the image of the endomorphism loops. This may be why he struck the formula out.

(3) Model-category side. On the right he writes 'M W', 'Hot', a crossed-out 'Ch_W(x,y) =' (chemins/chaînes) and 'Cl(M,W)' with 'Hom' struck out. The large drawing is two zigzags of arrows of alternating direction from x to y, upper and lower. This is exactly the picture of a hammock in the Dwyer–Kan hammock localization L^H(M,W) (1980): zigzags with backwards arrows in W, and 2-dimensional 'hammocks' connecting two zigzags. So he is weighing a direct construction of Homhot(x,y) from a category with weak equivalences (M,W) via zigzags, against the derivator-internal approach.

(4) Diagram variation. 'J⊂I, X_j, H(J), H(I,J), H(I)→H(J), X_i→X_j, Y_i→Y_j' concerns restriction along a subcategory J⊂I and a relative or pair version H(I,J). This is probably the relative underline-Homhot of page 1, or diagrams indexed by pairs.

The next page turns this into a programme for homotopy theories: models, long exact sequences, resolutions, Hom objects in Hot, 'chez Quillen il y a des Hom simpliciaux'.
errors: The tentative recovery of π1(Map(x,y),f) from the fibre of H(Δ1)→H(e)×H(e) is not exact. Automorphisms of the coherent arrow over (id_x,id_y) give π1(Map(x,y),f) only modulo the image of π1(Map(x,x)×Map(y,y)), and the identification also involves extension issues. Grothendieck struck out the formula, so no error is asserted on the page; it is an abandoned attempt.

ideas.what: Mapping homotopy type Homhot(x,y) of a derivator, with π0 = Hom and higher π_i to be read off from H(Δ1), H(Δ1×Δ1), …
ideas.modern_name: Hot-enrichment / mapping spaces of a derivator; derivators as shadows of (∞,1)-categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (Hot-enrichment of derivators, c. 2003–2008); Renaudin (2009); Lurie for the ∞-categorical framework
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (1990–91) treats derivators. Pursuing Stacks discusses Hom in Hot. This specific π1 attempt is not known to me in print.

ideas.what: Zigzags of arrows (backward arrows weak equivalences) from x to y and 2-dimensional fillings between two zigzags, as model for Hom in (M,W)
Homotopies between maps and homotopies between homotopies as cells x⇉y with ⇓ and ⇛
ideas.modern_name: 2-cells / higher cells of the mapping space

ideas.what: Restriction H(I)→H(J) for J⊂I and a pair version H(I,J)
ideas.modern_name: restriction functors of a derivator; relative or pair diagrams

deep.surprise_reason: These are mostly doodles exploring how to get mapping spaces from a derivator and from (M,W) via zigzags. The ideas (hammocks, Hot-enrichment of derivators) are known and credited to others. The page contains no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Hot' under 'M W' is written as 'Hbt'/'Hot'; it reads as Hot.
The crossed-out continuation of π1(x,y;f) = … appears to begin with something like 'Hom' or 'π0(Δ1…'; it is illegible.

Bottom right: 'Hom' (struck through) above 'Cl (M, W)'. The line below it is illegible: it begins with a word resembling 'morphismes' and continues with something like 'pas', so the reading is uncertain.
The large central-right drawing is a closed loop of two zigzags of alternately oriented arrows between x and y (a hammock picture), not just 'zigzag of arrows'.
'x ←→ y' at mid-left is x with an arrow to y (the left end has a small mark), probably a weak equivalence or an invertible arrow.
